stories.headline: Wyoming fossils revealed the 'fattest' squid relative ever
stories.summary: Most belemnite fossils in Wyoming are 1-2 cm wide. This new 160-million-year-old species is 6 cm across. A fossil collector found one of only 2 specimens and donated it.
stories.why: It belongs to a family scientists thought had died out millions of years earlier.

stories.headline: Astronomers measured the Big Bang's helium more precisely than ever
stories.summary: In 130 hours of telescope time, a team studied 15 untouched galaxies to measure the helium made in the universe's first 5 minutes, to within 0.5%.
stories.why: A lead astronomer called it one of the biggest findings of his 40-year career.

stories.headline: A soil microbe's weapon kills a dangerous gut bug and spares the good ones
stories.summary: Argyrin B, made by soil bacteria, cleared C. difficile in infected mice while barely touching helpful gut microbes. Taken by mouth, most of it stayed in the gut.
stories.why: It could one day spare patients repeat infections and even stool transplants.

stories.stat_label: freshwater cave snail found in China
stories.headline: China's 1st known cave snail has no eyes and a see-through shell
stories.summary: Found 2,062 m up in a Yunnan cave, the tiny snail lives in total darkness and hides from light. It's named after a faceless god from an ancient Chinese text.
stories.why: It's the highest cave snail of its family ever recorded.

fun_fact: The new 'squid' fossil's name, Wyoteuthis, simply means 'a squid from Wyoming'.
